title: Kastamonu
capsule: Kastamonu here denotes the Candarid (Jandarid) beylik of northern Anatolia, an Oghuz Turkic principality founded around 1291 when the Seljuk sultan Mesud II granted Eflani to Şemseddin Yaman Candar Bey for rescuing him from Mongol captivity. In the early fourteenth century, under Süleyman I Pasha (r. c. 1309–1339), the beylik expanded from its base to take the city of Kastamonu and reached the Black Sea at Sinop, all while ruling under the overlordship of the Mongol Ilkhanate. Süleyman's death around 1339 set off a succession struggle between his sons Ibrahim and Ali, with Ibrahim prevailing to rule Kastamonu into the mid-1340s.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The attestation window 1305–1344 captures only the early phase of the principality; the territorial core around Kastamonu is known, but exact extent in the Paphlagonian highlands at this period is poorly documented.
